Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia (heart shadow on the right) and a gastric bubble under the right hemidiaphragm, indicating situs inversus. Kartagener's syndrome is characterized by the triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis; thus, the finding of a left-sided liver (implied by the right-sided stomach/heart arrangement in situs inversus totalis) and right-sided heart supports this diagnosis.
